title: Investigation of α-V2O5 as a Cathode Material for Magnesium Ion Batteries Using Atomic Resolved Scanning Transmission Electron Microscopy
content: While Li-ion batteries face challenges related to energy density, safety, and resource availability, magnesium-based systems have emerged as a promising alternative due to the stability of Mg metal anodes, efficient multivalent ion transfer at the cathode, and the abundance of Mg resources [1]. Among potential cathode materials, transition metal (TM) oxides have gained significant interest for their ability to intercalate Mg²+, making them strong candidates for rechargeable batteries [2]. However, electrochemical cycling of these oxides with Mg²+ induces irreversible structural changes, leading to capacity and voltage fade [1].
